## 740d triage reversed a recorded disposition -- it is a genuine defect

The ticket carried two prior RCA comments concluding 'host-environment artifact, no code fix
warranted'. That is wrong, and the project's own history settles it without needing a judgement call.

Root cause: git refuses to DISCOVER a bare repo via -C/cwd when safe.bareRepository=explicit; it
accepts one named by top-level --git-dir. The _git helper in
tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py:40-46 hardcodes git -C <repo>, so the five
tests reading the bare fixture remote die with exit 128 BEFORE any ref lookup.

Two claims in the original report are false and were sending readers down dead ends:
 - 'refs/heads/tickets does not exist' -- it exists and resolves fine; git never gets that far.
 - 'git 2.55.0' -- safe.bareRepository shipped in git 2.38.0 (2022-10-03) with exactly these
   semantics. Four years stable. No version regression to chase.

Measured: 17 passed under default config isolated; 546 passed across the whole lifecycle directory;
5 failed / 12 passed under safe.bareRepository=explicit. No pollution, no ordering dependency -- one
config value governs the split entirely. Reproduced with an ordinary user gitconfig, no
GIT_CONFIG_COUNT injection, so it is not a harness artifact.

WHY IT IS A RECURRENCE, AND THE PART THAT MATTERS: closed ticket 3476-4472-3407-4246
(embolismic-adverse-dragon) fixed this exact class across 13 files and added the held-out oracle
tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py. It also recorded the policy
verbatim: 'the supported test suite must run both locally and in CI. Treat agents dismissing
reproducible local test failures as environmental noise as an anti-pattern.' The guard missed this
file because it pins a HARDCODED 3-entry _FIXTURE_NODES allowlist, and
test_atomic_completion_close.py landed 2026-08-25 (commit 1cb1cdd25aff) -- four days after the guard
and three days before 3476 closed. No static sweep exists anywhere (scripts/, Makefile,
.pre-commit-config.yaml); scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py covers an unrelated concern.

So fixing only the five call sites would leave exactly the gap that produced this recurrence. AC4
therefore targets the allowlist itself: the guard's coverage must be derived from the tree, or an
unregistered bare-fixture test must fail. This is the same lesson as the 2593 fix, where a
hard-coded module list was replaced by a tree-derived scan -- twice in one day a hand-maintained
allowlist silently stopped guarding.

Ticket retitled around safe.bareRepository=explicit, description rewritten with the measurements,
file_impact set to the two files, linked relates_to 3476, and the disposition correction recorded as
a comment. Fix subagent dispatched with both halves required and AC3's mutation proof mandatory.

CROSS-CUTTING LESSON now in every subagent brief: putting the worktree venv first on PATH is not
only about the commit hook resolving ruff/mypy -- it also determines WHICH REBAR BUILD evaluates a
gate. The global pipx rebar on this host is ~195 commits stale and its verdicts 'can be wrong in
ways the verdict cannot show'. Briefs now require confirming 'which rebar' resolves into the
worktree and reading the gate's own build_drift line before trusting a verdict.

## The stale global rebar was not normal -- the hourly updater has been dead for 119 runs

The user asked whether this environment has an auto-update keeping rebar in sync with origin/main.
It does, and it is BROKEN. I had treated the 195-commits-behind global build as an ambient fact and
merely routed around it; it is actually a five-day outage of the update mechanism, affecting every
session on this host.

Filed ae97-a37b-9fa3-413a / princely-courageous-milksnake, priority 1.

ROOT CAUSE -- an inverted assumption, not a missing upgrade.
rebar-dev-update.sh:18 hardcodes UV_BIN=${REBAR_DEV_UV_BIN:-/opt/homebrew/bin/uv}, and :120 orders
PATH to keep Homebrew authoritative with the stated reason at :116-118: 'Keep Homebrew before
~/.local/bin so the obsolete standalone uv there cannot shadow the pinned UV_BIN.' Measured today:
/opt/homebrew/bin/uv is 0.12.6 (2026-08-25); /Users/joeoakhart/.local/bin/uv is 0.12.7 (2026-08-27).
The premise inverted -- Homebrew is now the stale side -- so the guard written to prevent selecting
a stale uv is the mechanism selecting one. pyproject.toml:346 pins required-version = '==0.12.7',
uv reads it itself and fails fast, so every hourly 'uv sync' aborts. 118 of 119 rejections are this;
one is a transient fetch-pack early EOF at the checkout stage.

SAME PIN, THIRD CONSUMER. required-version '==0.12.7' (commit 7501cc1d602d) is the same pin whose
floating uv:latest Dockerfile tags caused the multi-hour MCP outage under bug febd. That fix pinned
the three infra/compose Dockerfiles and extended scripts/check_uv_pin.py to scan them. This host's
updater is a third consumer that was never brought along -- and it is out of check_uv_pin.py's reach
because it is a machine-local, git-ignored script. Linked relates_to febd.

THE DETECTION GAP IS THE WORSE HALF. docs/local-env-main-tracking.local.md documents a
REJECT_STREAK_ALERT (default 3) added after 'the b477339a99 incident: 43 hourly sync rejections,
~48 commits behind, no signal'. That alert is firing correctly every hour and failing to deliver
every time: AuthorizationError, IAM user in account 820258254566 publishing to an SNS topic in
account 896586841071, no resource-based policy permitting it. Streak 119 against a threshold of 3,
zero operator signal -- a strictly worse recurrence of the exact incident the alert exists to
prevent. So AC4 requires a LOCAL detector that does not depend on the remote sink at all.

IMPACT WORTH BEING BLUNT ABOUT: any plan-review or completion-verifier verdict produced through the
global rebar on this host in the last five days used a build whose own advisory says results 'can
be wrong in ways the verdict cannot show'. That is not limited to this session.

Secondary: launchd.err.log shows the pruner failing with 'Directory not empty' on release dirs, and
releases/5fb693345b0c...1559 is a 3-entry stub from a partially built release. At ~346 MB per
release dir this is disk-ceiling relevant, so linked relates_to epic 6202.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER FRAMING: I told a subagent to use the worktree venv 'because the global
build is stale'. That was the right instruction for the wrong reason -- I presented a broken
updater as a standing environmental condition. The venv-on-PATH rule remains correct regardless,
but the staleness itself is a bug with a ticket, not a fact of the environment.

comments.body:
## Closing lesson: tick the AC boxes ONLY -- adding prose to the description at close time breaks the attestation

S0's close was blocked twice, both times correctly, and the second block taught something worth
keeping.

BLOCK 1 -- unchecked acceptance criteria. The completion gate refused because all six '- [ ]' items
were still unticked. It offered --force; not used. Verified all six against the ADR AS MERGED on
origin/main at 85ef5ad33ada rather than against intent: Option A (decision 1) and Option C
(decision 3) recorded; the PID+heartbeat lease documented as spiked and 'rejected as unsound';
decision 4 'Root stays 60 GiB -- that is headroom, not the fix' with the measurement that 60 GiB
fills as readily as 30 and only changes how long the fuse is; per-generator alarm precedent via
rebar-gerrit-data-disk-debris; external native-GC precedents Gitaly, Sourcegraph gitserver, Bazel,
ccache, Docker overlay2/BuildKit; and the commit touching exactly three files. All six genuinely
held, so ticking them was reporting a fact, not satisfying a gate.

BLOCK 2 -- and this is the reusable lesson. Alongside ticking the boxes I appended a short
explanatory blockquote to the description. The close then failed 'stale-material', and the gate's
message is unusually precise and worth quoting:

  'its TEXT changed, and checkbox state changed too (0 -> 6 ticked), which is NOT the cause; note
   that ticking an AC checkbox is attestation-SAFE (box state is normalized out of the fingerprint),
   so a tick is never the cause.'

So: checkbox state is deliberately normalized out of the plan fingerprint precisely so a close can
tick boxes without invalidating the attestation. ANY OTHER description edit at close time does
invalidate it and forces a fresh 15-20 minute review-plan. RULE: at close, tick boxes and change
nothing else; put closing evidence in a COMMENT. Removing the 231-character note restored the text
to the reviewed baseline (6997 -> 6998 chars, a trailing newline) and cleared stale-material.

Note also the gate diagnosed the cause for me instead of just reporting staleness -- it distinguished
the text change from the tick change and pre-emptively ruled the tick out. That is a good failure
message and the reason this cost minutes rather than a wasted gate run.

REMAINING QUESTION, being tested by the third close attempt: 'review-plan --status' still reports
stale-code, because the three file_impact paths changed -- which is S0's OWN work landing. With
currency_basis=file_impact that appears to be the normal end state of every completed ticket. If the
close gate enforced stale-code, no ticket carrying file_impact could ever close without re-running
plan review, so it presumably does not. Worth confirming empirically rather than assuming, which is
what the current attempt does.

## c379 triaged: a genuine defect that an ACCEPTED ADR already settled the other way

Classification: genuine defect, reproducible on current origin/main (7d3907101dd6), not fixed since
filing. Fix agent dispatched.

MECHANISM -- a dead conjunct. next_batch.py:262 already excludes every structural container via
parent_ids_with_children (built at :162). The branch at :264-267 guards on
'ttype == "story" and tid not in parent_ids_with_children', whose SECOND CONJUNCT IS DEAD because
line 262 guarantees it. So it reduces to 'type == story => never schedulable'. Worse, the rendered
reason at :405-407 -- 'needs implementation planning (story has 0 children)' -- asserts an inference
nothing verifies: the branch never consults plan-review state, so a childless story holding a current
CERTIFIED plan-review PASS still reports as unplanned.

The asymmetry is the clean falsification: under one epic, a childless EPIC is batched and a childless
BUG is batched; only a childless STORY is vetoed. Whatever 'stories are containers' would mean, it
cannot survive a childless epic being schedulable.

THE PROJECT ALREADY DECIDED THIS. docs/adr/0078-plan-review-container-leaf-scrutiny.md (Accepted):
'Proportionate scrutiny is keyed on container (has children) vs leaf (no children), NEVER on ticket

## S1 merged; its close failed on MY error, and the gate caught it

Change 2620 merged as bb65f47becfe 'Isolate review-gate scratch on its own EBS volume', carrying
rebar-ticket: aa40. Twelve changes merged tonight.

THE CLOSE FAILED, correctly: 'it records file_impact but no commit references it'. My error -- I ran
the close from S6'S worktree, not S1's. That worktree had diverged (it held S6's own commit), so my
'git merge --ff-only origin/main' FAILED, leaving HEAD eleven commits behind, and I chained the close
after it without checking the ff had succeeded. Fixed by resetting that worktree to origin/main (its
work is merged, nothing lost) and verifying reachability explicitly before retrying:
'git merge-base --is-ancestor bb65f47becfe HEAD' -> YES, and
'rebar verify-commit-ticket --rev bb65f47becfe' -> OK - resolved aa40.

That is the FOURTH time tonight I assumed a command's effect instead of verifying it -- after the
blind monitor, the patchset-base filter, and dispatching test.yml into a running job. Each time a gate
or a later check caught it rather than me. Worth stating plainly: the gates in this repo are doing
real work, and several of tonight's 'good catches' were catches of MY mistakes, not the tree's.

S1'S TWO SUBSTANTIVE FINDINGS, recorded on the ticket so a future simplifying edit cannot undo them:
 - REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR takes TWO env vars, not one. It moves the content-addressed store, but the
   review-bot's per-review clone is a plain tempfile.TemporaryDirectory following TMPDIR -- and that
   clone is the path whose bytes scale LINEARLY WITH CONCURRENCY. Setting only the first is half a fix.
 - An unmounted volume RAISES NOTHING. A mount point whose volume is absent is an ordinary, writable,
   EMPTY directory, so mkdir(parents=True) silently recreates the store on root and every gate keeps
   working on the disk the epic protects. S6's fail-closed-on-OSError cannot see it because there is
   no error. Hence two markers on two different filesystems: declaration on root (survives unmount),
   proof on the volume (vanishes with it); only declaration-present + proof-absent refuses.

And patchset 2 fixed a perfect inversion in its own patchset 1: the recovery runbook said 'touch
<mount>/.gate-scratch-mounted', which while unmounted lands on ROOT and tells the guard the volume is
present. THE RECOVERY PROCEDURE FOR THE SILENT FALLBACK WOULD HAVE PERFORMED THE SILENT FALLBACK.

FILED 1ef8-c849-5801-4eee (fillable-starry-aruanas, p1): the refusal guards gate_admission(), which
the review-bot clone path does not pass through -- so on a declared-but-unmounted volume the gates
refuse loudly while the review-bot clones onto root quietly. A PARTIAL refusal is arguably worse than
none, because the loud half creates confidence the protection is in force. Needs ADR 0069
retryable-deferral so it never becomes a false LLM-Review -1 against an innocent change.
